data.message: The request JSON contains a key that is not a recognised slot of the object it sits in — at the request root or at any depth (a sort entry, an aggregation, a crosstab cell, a Compose slot, a chain stage, a sweep body, a for_each item). Every JSON request root (CLI request files, MCP tool arguments, Compose sweep bodies and for_each items) is decoded strictly, so the key is refused rather than ignored: an ignored key would silently drop the intended operation. A slot this instance's feature profile hides is refused the same way and is never listed as valid. A common cause is using a manifest operator-catalog field name ("groupers", "aggregators") as the request key instead of the request slot name ("groups", "aggregations"). Below the root `details.path` locates the first offending key ("sort[0].direction", "aggregations[0].weight") and `valid_keys` lists that object's keys; `details.request` / `fit` / `stage` (Compose slot, fit, chain stage) or `slot` (sweep) / `index` (for_each combination) say which nested request it is in. Synth documents decode the same way: a spec, a `--rules` file (its file in `details.file`) or a profile document refuses an unknown key, and a spec field's `params` refuses a key its distribution does not read (`fields[0].params.rate` → `lambda`); correlation entries are `{a, b, rho}`.

fixups.hint: Rename the offending key to its canonical request slot: the error details carry the nearest valid key under suggestions and every slot this instance accepts under valid_keys. The manifest's "groupers"/"aggregators" name the available OPERATORS; the request slots that hold them are "groups"/"aggregations".
